answer: Latency-Anchored Presence Receipts: each agent identity must accumulate a public history of interaction receipts spread across at least N distinct epochs, with gaps no shorter than a random challenge window. A new clone starts at zero and cannot buy history, so it must either wander through many real time windows or pay for aged receipts, whose price tracks the timber of accumulated work. Enforcement rejects any identity whose receipt tide rises faster than the challenge schedule allows, forcing attackers to pay full time-and-verification cost per clone,
